clue.text: Source of leverage secure, acquiring Shard?

parts.note: to secure a door is to bar it
acquiring means gaining, getting hold of
a shard is a broken fragment, a chip

explanation.surface: A question about whether bagging the London skyscraper, the Shard, would give someone leverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shard' looks like the London tower, but it is just a splinter or fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offered or held back in negotiations gives one side leverage over the other.

clue.text: Faff about stuffing crumbs into Brent goose prepared for main course

indicators.note: Faff about tells us those four letters are jumbled
the letters of faff are broken up and pushed in among the others like crumbs of stuffing
the goose is prepared, its letters worked into a new dish

explanation.surface: A cook fusses over stuffing breadcrumbs into a Brent goose before serving it as the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole fodder FAFF plus BRENTGOOSE is rearranged; the Brent goose is a small wild goose, here just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This Russian dish of sliced beef in a sour-cream sauce is served as an entrée or principal dish.

clue.text: To and fro in circle dance?

parts.note: a round is a circle
to trip is to dance lightly, as in 'trip the light fantastic'

explanation.surface: Dancers move back and forth in a ring, as in a folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey there and back again is travel to and fro.

clue.text: Plug Steel, perhaps, extempore?

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement or ad
David Steel led the British Liberal Party, so he is an example of a Lib

explanation.surface: Was the advert for steel made up on the spot?
explanation.walkthrough: David Steel was leader of the Liberal Party in the UK; LIB is short for Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking extempore means improvising without preparation, which is to speak off the cuff.

clue.text: Band drink on stage, incessantly

parts.note: to neck a drink is British slang for downing it quickly

indicators.note: without ceasing, read as 'without its end', so the last letter of the stage word goes

parts.note: a tier is a level or stage

explanation.surface: A band drinks constantly while on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians but is a strip of cloth worn round the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a strip or band of fabric worn around the collar.

clue.text: With engagement cancelled, learnt painfully about 'elite'

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the elite letter
painfully suggests the letters of learnt are twisted and wrenched about

parts.note: U stands for upper class, the elite

explanation.surface: Someone whose engagement was called off learnt a painful lesson about the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' looks romantic, but it is the meshing of gears; out of gear the car is in neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: When a gearbox is disengaged, no gear meshes with the drive, which is the neutral position.

clue.text: See 1
Crowd fund announced?

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so we want a word sounding like the fund word

parts.note: a hoard is a stockpile or fund of something

explanation.surface: A crowdfunding campaign is announced.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large, unruly mass of people, a throng.

clue.text: Berry's split accommodation charge

parts.note: a peppercorn is the dried berry of the pepper plant
rent is a past tense of rend, so it means split or torn

explanation.surface: Someone called Berry splits the cost of their lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Berry looks like a name; it is the pepper fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal, token sum paid as a lease payment for property is called by this name.

clue.text: Brown — Treasury fanatic?

parts.note: a treasury can be a chest where valuables are kept
a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown, former Chancellor, as a Treasury obsessive.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown suggests Gordon Brown, UK Chancellor of the Exchequer and so head of the Treasury; it is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: This reddish-brown shade is named after the nut of the sweet tree.

clue.text: Peer's plaque quietly removed and replaced

indicators.note: removed says the quiet letter is taken away from the plaque
replaced means the remaining letters are put back in a different order

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A lord's commemorative plaque is quietly taken down and swapped for another.
explanation.walkthrough: Peer looks like a lord; here it is one's equal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is someone of the same standing or rank, a match for another.

clue.text: Tablet — yuck! — medic popped in box

indicators.note: popped in means placed inside

parts.note: a coop is a box-like cage for hens
ugh is an exclamation of disgust like yuck
DR is short for doctor

explanation.surface: A patient finds a pill disgusting after a doctor tucks it into a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge for soothing the throat is a small medicinal tablet.

clue.text: Expert: 'Flatfish season's not quite finished'

parts.note: dabs are small flatfish

indicators.note: not quite finished means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a term is a period or season

explanation.surface: An expert pronounces that the flatfish season has not yet ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabster is an old word, still used in British dialect, for an adept or someone skilled.

clue.text: Hide's converted, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is listened to, not read

parts.note: to be swayed is to be talked round, converted to a view

explanation.surface: Someone's hiding place has been converted, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is a kind of leather, an animal skin, with a napped finish.

clue.text: See 1
Meat Loaf's entire recordings initially misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced means the letters have been put in the wrong positions
initially picks just the opening letter of recordings

explanation.surface: The singer Meat Loaf has lost his entire back catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Meat Loaf looks like the rock singer, but it is a dish of pressed meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This French dish is a coarse pâté baked in an earthenware mould, much like a pressed loaf of meat.

clue.text: 'Sweet!' one cries aloud

indicators.note: aloud means the words are spoken and heard

parts.note: one cries can be put as 'I scream'

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out in delight, 'Sweet!'
explanation.walkthrough: Echoes the rhyme 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream'.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert counts as a sweet, the British word for a pudding course.

clue.text: Disturbed one among the French having spasm

indicators.note: among means set in the middle of the article

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
'un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'
a tic is an involuntary twitch or spasm

explanation.surface: A troubled person among the French is having a fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing someone as mad or mentally unhinged is the old informal sense of disturbed.

clue.text: Bobby occupies run-down let — see contract

indicators.note: occupies means moves into and sits inside
run-down suggests the letters are dilapidated and disordered

parts.note: a bobby is a British policeman, a cop

explanation.surface: A policeman moves into a shabby rented flat; see the tenancy agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun, a lease; it is the verb, to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten by sliding sections together, like a collapsible spyglass, is to contract.

clue.text: Late news Stone missed in crush

indicators.note: missed in the sense of left out or skipped over, so the weight unit is dropped from the news phrase

parts.note: stop press is late news added to a newspaper after printing has begun
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A late news story reports that a man named Stone was missed in a crowd crush.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to subdue or keep down harshly, as a tyrant crushes a people.

clue.text: Indication my MP's to get sacked

indicators.note: sacked suggests the letters are thrown out and scattered, as when a town is sacked

explanation.surface: Someone sees a sign that their MP is about to be fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign or token that points to a condition, especially an illness.

clue.text: Token 'bird' goes to heart of popularism

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: heart of takes the central letters of popularism

explanation.surface: A token bird is placed at the centre of a populist campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Titular means in name only, nominal, as a token figurehead is.

clue.text: Curl's split end riled somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by a split end in their curl.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a thin coiling shoot or lock, a curl; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Oil and salt on a beetroot?

indicators.note: in a down-the-page reading, salt on something comes after it, so the sailor follows

parts.note: read as beet's root, the bottom or last letter of the word beet
an old salt is a sailor, a tar

explanation.surface: Dressing a beetroot with oil and salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt on' places the sailor after the A and the final letter of beet.
explanation.definitionFit: Attar is a fragrant essential oil made from rose petals.

clue.text: Third rail 25 moving in and out

indicators.note: the solution to 25 down, meaning in an odd way, tells us to take the odd letters

explanation.surface: The third rail of an electric railway, live current moving in and out.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of 'Third rail' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea rising and falling with the tide flows in and out of a shore or estuary.

clue.text: Trees woodman turns to wood — thus?

indicators.note: the clue asks what instruction makes the woodcutter's word become just wood, and the answer split in two is that instruction

parts.note: the starting word, whose male figure departs to leave wood

explanation.surface: A woodcutter is transformed into timber, a fairytale fate.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer split as MAN GOES, applied to woodman, leaves wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Mango plants are tropical fruit-bearing evergreen trees.

clue.text: Unaccountably swallowed too much alcohol — jury's conclusions

parts.note: OD'd, written ODD, is short for overdosed, having swallowed too much of a drug

indicators.note: conclusions picks the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A juror inexplicably drank too much, and the verdict was strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening strangely or inexplicably happens in a peculiar way.

clue.text: See 8
Lotto, say, and chips?

definitions.meaning: Lorenzo Lotto was a great painter of the Italian Renaissance
Mr Chips, of 'Goodbye, Mr Chips', is an aged schoolteacher

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lotto' looks like a lottery game and 'chips' like fried potatoes or gambling tokens.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are an eminent painter of the pre-modern era and also an elderly teacher.

clue.text: Monotonous speech given by rambling De Niro I missed

indicators.note: rambling means the letters wander about out of order
missed tells us the single letter goes from the actor's name

explanation.surface: Robert De Niro gives a rambling, dull speech and I missed it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a low, monotonous hum, hence a tedious way of speaking.

clue.text: Satisfied workers, in Ptolemy's interpretation, creating an ideal economic state of affairs

parts.note: full means satisfied after eating

indicators.note: in means placed inside the rearranged letters
an interpretation is a rendering, so the name's letters are rendered anew

parts.note: men are workers, hands

explanation.surface: Satisfied workers, as the astronomer Ptolemy might have seen it, make for an ideal economy.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation where everyone who wants a job has one is the goal of economic policy.
